title: How a reversible transition amplifies apparent entropy production
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. Small driven systems such as molecular motors, ion channels and colloidal beads in moving traps turn part of the energy they receive into heat; the rate of this entropy production is a basic thermodynamic quantity. Experiments usually see only a few transitions and the waiting times between them, so a large literature derives lower bounds on dissipation from waiting-time statistics.

Question. For periodically driven systems, Harunari, Fiore and Barato (Physical Review E, 2024) proposed a practical estimator S1: record the waiting times between visible jumps once with the driving protocol and once with the protocol reversed, without recording the phase of the drive, and compare the two histograms. They proved that S1 minus a correction X is a lower bound on the entropy production σ, and left open whether S1 alone is one.

Main results. (1) The uncorrected estimate is not a lower bound, and its excess is unbounded. In a smooth three-state model with zero period-averaged current on every edge, equal event rates in both experiments and fixed entropy production 4π/5, the estimate grows linearly with the rate R of one reversible transition. An exact rational certificate proves S1 > 31σ at R = 105, and a certified lag-bin bound gives S1 > 145σ; the smallest certified violation is at R = 750, about 375 reporter events per period. (2) The failure persists when every microscopic jump is recorded, and under a small constant cycle affinity, under which the model numerically pumps a net current. (3) For every finite driven network, the estimate from blocks of m consecutive waits exceeds the phase-resolved bound by at most X/m, where X needs only the phase histogram of each kind of visible event; the coefficient of X/m cannot be lowered. If visible events sample the phase reversal-symmetrically (X = 0), the uncorrected estimate is safe. (4) In the example, the block estimate is determined in every scaling regime, with a transition at blocks of order R2/3 waits.

Relation to earlier work. This is a follow-up to the Evidence Press release Counterexamples to a conjectured waiting-time bound on entropy production in periodically driven Markov networks (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23541298), which refuted a related forward-only conjecture of Maier, Degünther, van der Meer and Seifert. Harunari, Fiore and Barato's corrected inequality σ ≥ S1 − X remains valid; it is the case m = 1 of the block theorem.

Limits. A model calculation, with no claim about a particular experiment. The overshoot per event is small (under 0.008 nats per event) and needs a reporter several hundred times faster than the drive. The scaling table and the sharpness statement are proved for the example only; the net current under a cycle affinity is numerical, not proved. Whether S1 ≤ σ holds throughout Harunari, Fiore and Barato's own pump model remains open, and finite-sample estimation is not analysed.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF); three certificate scripts in exact integer and rational arithmetic (standard library); four floating-point illustrations (NumPy, SciPy); the error analysis of the bin certificates; recorded outputs; the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Every check exits with an error on failure, also under python -O.

Assurance. Written proofs with exact rational certificates. Internal AI-assisted review only: a five-role Claude review panel, the lead's replay of the exact rational certificates with negative controls, one revision round with extensions, then a re-review and proof audit of the new proofs, which corrected a threshold in Corollary 3 to R ≥ 5400 (checked exactly). No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
